_doc: Features read off the Wright 1834 sheet EAST of the current terrain box, to scope and then build S2e (see docs/ROADMAP.md). Pixel readings are the evidence and are committed as such; local ENU is derived from them by tools/wright_px.py using the same fitted affine tools/rederive_datum.py checks the datum against, so nothing here is a second georeference. Read BY EYE at the stated resolution — these are fair estimates in the sense docs/PROVENANCE.md now licenses, not survey-grade traces.
cross_check: The Fort Dearborn reading lands at local E +1152, N +221. An independent estimate from the modern successor landmark (Michigan Avenue bridge, via EPSG:26916) gives E +1127, N +195 — 35 m apart, inside the sheet's own +/-20 m plus the ambiguity of which point either method names. Two methods that do not share an input agreeing at that distance is the reason this is tagged inferred rather than conjectural.

lake_shore_north_of_harbour.what_was_read: the WEST edge of the grey coastal wash. Wright shades the lake as a band that fades east, so the wash edge is the shoreline and the pale ground beyond it is still lake, not land.

harbour_north_pier.what_was_read: the inner of the two red pier lines running ENE from the river mouth.

fort_dearborn_label.what_was_read: centre of the FORT DEARBORN banner. Wright LABELS the reservation and does not draw the fort's plan, so this fixes the place, not the footprint — the palisade outline must come from elsewhere.

river_mouth_south_bank.what_was_read: south bank at the cut, where the channel meets the harbour works.
